newsitem.title: NORWAY: Bergesen sees better 96 operating profit than 95.
newsitem.headline: Bergesen sees better 96 operating profit than 95.

text.p: Norway's biggest shipping company, Bergesen d.y. ASA, said on Thursday it expected 1996 operating profits to improve on the 1995 comparative figures, but that pre-tax profits would be lower.

The group said nine-month operating profits rose to 308 million crowns from 253 million in the same year-ago period because of a sharply reduced loss in the tanker business to 39 million crowns from 191 million in the red.
"Bergesen's 1996 operating profit as a whole will show an improvement from 1995," a statement said. "Pre-tax profits will, however, show a decrease compared to the previous year."

Operating revenue rose to 3.37 billion crowns from 3.19 billion but the pre-tax result shrank to 97 million crowns from 366 million. Analysts had expected a pre-tax profit of 208 million crowns for the first nine months.

"The spot and time/charter market for the largest gas carriers are expected to continue to improve in the fourth quarter. This will have a positive influence on the rate level for other gas segments, in particular the 50,000-60,000 cbm segment," it said.
The fourth-quarter tanker market is expected to stay on a par with the level seen at the start of the quarter, Bergesen said.

"This means rates which are weaker than those seen in the third quarter. The dry bulk market is expected to improve somewhat in the fourth quarter, in connection with an improved winter market," it said.
